newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian state stake in UES to fall to 50 pct.
newsitem.headline: Russian state stake in UES to fall to 50 pct.

text.p: A decree authorising Russia's Unified Energy System (UES) to issue convertible bonds foresees the state's stake in the national power utility falling to 50 percent plus one share, chief executive Boris Brevnov said on Thursday.

The federal government currently has a 52.7 percent stake in RAO Yedinaya Energeticheskaya Sistema Rossii (UES). On Wednesday President Boris Yeltsin signed a decree authorising UES to issue five trillion roubles of convertible bonds.
Brevnov told reporters that a tender to choose managers for the issue would be announced next week and held in the next three weeks.
The amount of shares to be covered by the bond has not yet been set, he said.
Fifteen percent of UES's authorised capital has not been issued as shares and up to 2.3 percent of company-controlled capital could be earmarked for the bond programme.
With the 2.7 pct released by the reduction in the government's stake, this would take the total to five percent.
Shareholders will vote on the bonds on August 26. The company also plans an American Depositary Receipt (ADR) programme to allow its shares to trade abroad before the bonds.
At 0925 GMT UES stock was at $0.4281, in a generally weaker Russian market, after closing on Thursday at $0.4320.
